title: Kumar 1988: centroid distance of lateral abdominal wall pooled at T12 (M, supine)

imaging.plane: transverse CT slices (gantry plane) at the vertebral body; centres located by geometric construction (ellipse/apex lines), not area centroids
imaging.level_definition: vertebral body level (T7, T12, L3, L5)

quantity.name: centroid_distance
quantity.definition: distance from the vertebral-body (or disc) centroid to the muscle area centroid in the image plane; AP signed (+ anterior, - posterior), ML unsigned lateral distance. NOT a true moment arm

source.sample: 56 patients (35 M, 21 F); per level T7 20, T12 41, L3 32, L5 13; archival CT of patients without musculoskeletal disorders

protocol.summary: Archival supine CT; lever arms from geometric muscle centres to vertebral body centre, pooled right and left.
how_to_simulate: Cut a transverse plane through the T12 vertebral body.
Take the PCSA-weighted centroid of combined obliques on each side; reference = vertebral body centre (intersection of the spinous-process midline and the widest coronal line).
Report perpendicular distance to the coronal line (AP) and to the midsagittal line (ML); average right and left (the paper pooled both sides).
Note: muscle "centres" were geometric (axes/apex constructions), not area centroids.
protocol.notes: Authors call these moment arms (lever arms); they are centroid distances. Older clinical population. cm -> mm. Trunk diameters (Table 9) not stored.

extraction.check_notes: All table values re-read from text; OCR artefacts (IO.37 -> 10.37, o-45 -> 0.45, l-04 -> 1.04, 11 .oo -> 11.00) corrected by reading the digits.
